The current Toreador Justicar, Madame Guil has held the post for some time and wields her power well. She is just as prone to using her authority to fulfill her private agendas as any other justicar, but she has also been known to destroy princes in her efforts to maintain the Masquerade and uphold the other Traditions. Rumor holds she employs a few Ventrue archons in her service, as well as others from more disparate clans.

Her ongoing rivalry with the Tremere Justicar, Anastasz di Zagreb, has made for some painful clashes between the two clans, and any Toreador operating in Camarilla circles is likely to feel the ripples of that feud sooner or later.

Katherine of Montpellier is the legendary originator of Soul Painting, the ancient Toreador art of capturing a subject's inner nature within a portrait. Her technique flourished briefly in the early 1300s before her presumed Final Death, but in recent nights she has returned, roused from an ages-long torpor.

Katherine has agreed to teach a few worthy students her methods, though convincing her to take on a new pupil is no simple task. A prospective student must first impress her with a work of his own craft, for only those with adequate craftsmanship and sufficient insight have any chance of mastering the technique. Furthermore, the student must agree to obey Katherine in every particular — sometimes to the extent of taking two drinks toward a blood bond. Few are willing to apply under such terms, and of those, only a minority are judged skilled enough for instruction. Her most famous work, a portrait of the late Archbishop Monçada, reputedly took over one thousand hours to complete.
